subject: voice-io
note: Two engines behind one dispatcher implement opposite answers to the load-bearing arm. Kokoro (kokoro.rs:190) errors on an explicit-and-unmatched voice - the rule verbatim. Pocket falls through to the HTTP service, which resolves the name against a different catalog. Reachable by a normal action: companion_tts_pocket_delete_voice removes the .wav, nothing clears companionPocketVoiceId, configured stays true. Pocket is the CLONING engine, so the fall-through speaks in an unrequested voice after the caller named a specific person's clone. The frontend's terminal arm (athenaChatAudio.ts:64,91) is a silent return, not an error; there is no global default voice at all.
return_condition: start the Pocket service and POST a nonexistent voice id - if it already rejects distinguishably, only the frontend's silent arm is the defect

subject: voice-io
note: Ran the technique's detector (bounded internal silence enclosed on both sides by speech) over six REAL renders reproducing kokoro.rs's exact sidecar invocation. Longest internal gap across the whole corpus: 160 ms, including a 65.75 s render at the validator's own 1200-char ceiling and the technique's named false-positive case (a paced list). Any bound tuned from the legitimate side lands at 300 ms or above and fires zero times. Kokoro is a duration-predictor model with no stop condition to miss - the technique's own generative-engine precondition is false. Worse: the two degenerate outputs personas CAN reach (text '...' gives 0.17 s; text '###' gives the model reading hashes aloud) both pass the detector cleanly and are accepted by validate_text. Artifacts: .ai/apply-2026-09-03/{detect.py,render.sh,results.txt,renders/}.
return_condition: re-run detect.py against a Pocket TTS corpus - pocket.rs is autoregressive and IS the engine that can miss a stop condition; the verdict is per-engine and may invert

subject: sidecar-provisioning
note: The payload is already cut on the right seam (sherpa-onnx v1.13.4 engine on the toolchain clock; kokoro-multi-lang-v1_0 model, 325 MB + 27 MB measured on disk, on the tts-models clock) and carries none of the identity the cut requires. Both staleness predicates are presence, not version, so bumping ENGINE_ARCHIVE_URL changes nothing for an existing install, silently and forever. The model version is a documented correctness dependency (:36-37, v1_1 may reorder speakers). And two acquisition paths hold two InflightGuards keyed by INSTALLER while extracting the SAME engine archive into the SAME shared engine_dir() - the technique's named check-then-act race, reachable because the two panels compute showAutoInstall independently from two status calls.
return_condition: when a second sherpa-onnx version ships in a release, the presence predicate's silence becomes observable as a user stuck on a stale engine

subject: packaging
note: Amendment: attestation does not nest. The release's only cryptographic coverage is the minisign updater signature over UPDATER artifacts; tauri.conf.json:82 signingIdentity=null and :99 certificateThumbprint=null, so nothing is code-signed or notarized. bundle.targets=all also publishes the .dmg, .msi and NSIS .exe - the assets a first-time user downloads - and the gate's grep list (:459-467) matches none of them. The amendment's hard-fail-on-zero-inputs rule is already implemented here, with a good comment, over the wrong input set; the identity trap (:381-385) is already avoided. B is widening one grep list plus a verification call.
return_condition: run the widened enumeration on the next release - it should fail, because .dmg/.msi have no signature to find; if it passes, signing was added elsewhere
